quick_skim.title: Controlling Variability in~Neuroimaging Analysis Pipelines with~Software Product Lines
quick_skim.abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is an acquisition technique used for medical diagnosis. It is notably used for structural and functional MRI (or fMRI) image analysis. MRI data is known to be complex and noisy, so pipelines are created to extract and enhance relevant information in retrieved images. The NARPS study highlighted the significant variability that can emerge from different pipelines set up by independent teams while trying to answer the same research question about brain functioning. Having different implementations realizing the same task is a typical playground for software product lines (SPLs), which may be out of the sight of neuroimage practitioners. Thus, proposing an SPL out of these different pipelines falls back on a typical reverse-engineering problem with its usual difficulties. In this document, we advocate for the conceptual adoption of SPL principles as a promising direction to improve reproducibility and consistency in neuroimaging research.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: This paper addresses variability across MRI and fMRI analysis pipelines by modeling alternative implementations as a software product line, using NARPS evidence to argue that SPLs can control pipeline variability and improve reproducibility; it is neuroimaging-focused but not AI or connectivity modeling.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 针对MRI和fMRI数据复杂、不同团队分析流程差异导致结果变异的问题，提出用软件产品线方法组织神经影像分析流程，将多种实现视为可管理变体。文章结合NARPS研究说明流程选择对脑功能结论的影响，并论证SPL有助于控制变异性、提升可复现性。该工作直接面向神经影像与fMRI分析流程，但不涉及AI诊断、功能连接或双曲几何。

quick_skim.title: Phase-based Edge Coupling: Modeling Overlapping Functional Architectures and High-Order Edge-to-Edge Interactions in EEG Networks
quick_skim.abstract: Network neuroscience has traditionally relied on node-centric approaches, which are inherently limited in capturing the brain's overlapping functional architectures and higher-order edge-to-edge interactions. The emerging edge-centric paradigm addresses this gap by shifting the analytical unit from nodes to edges. However, while edge-centric models have been established for DTI and fMRI, comparable EEG methodologies have yet to be developed. In this study, we proposed a Phase-based Edge-centric Coupling (PEC) algorithm for EEG network modelling, where edge time series are derived from instantaneous phase differences of EEG signals and edge-to-edge coupling is quantified via normalized inner product. Simulation tests demonstrated the robustness of PEC algorithm, achieving high accuracy (<10% relative error) in coupling estimation and discriminative capacity (AUROC>0.7) against spurious coupling.When provided sufficient data length(>=16 cycles), PEC outperformed traditional Phase Node-centric Coupling (PNC) in both individual identifiability and cognitive-state identifiability, enabling superior characterization of stable individual neural signatures and dynamic task-dependent functional configurations. Furthermore, unlike PNC's hard-partitioned modularity, PEC captured highly overlapping yet functionally specialized modular structures and connector hubs, aligning with task-engaged cognitive processes. Applied to dyadic interactions, PEC identified distinct cross-brain modules encoding symmetric and asymmetric neural coordination. These findings establish PEC as a valid and powerful tool for EEG network modelling, providing new insights into the brain's complex, multifunctional organization at both intra-brain and inter-brain networks.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 该文针对传统节点中心方法难以刻画脑功能架构重叠与边间高阶交互的问题，指出现有边中心模型仅适用于DTI和fMRI而缺乏EEG方法。作者提出基于相位的边中心耦合算法PEC，由EEG瞬时相位差构建边时间序列并用归一化内积量化边间耦合。研究展示该方法可捕捉EEG网络的重叠功能架构与高阶交互。其贡献在于将边中心功能连接范式拓展到EEG，为脑网络分析提供新工具。
